body: Graceful hub stop via the child stdin pipe (hub --stop-on-stdin stops on EOF) instead of a stop file or an authenticated TCP/HTTP request: only the parent can trigger it, no secret needed, and a hard-killed supervisor still closes the pipe.

Holding stdin inside tokio::process::Child failed: Child::wait() closes the stdin it holds, so every hub stopped right after start (stdin closed; hub stopping). ChildStdin is now taken out and kept in Running.
Candidate "differs" check compares file bytes with the running binary instead of a hash or the --version string (version is 0.1.0 for every build; no hash crate in the agreed set).

Fake Telegram for the real-process test via a new optional CCTG_BOT_API_URL (BotApi::with_api_url already existed) rather than a test-only binary or skipping the hub; alternative was testing supervise against a stand-in hub program only.

Verdict NEEDS_WORK rather than PASS: all ACs are covered and tests are green, but a failed swap_in never withdraws cctg.next.exe, giving a hub restart loop and a later silent install after deploy reported failed; plus the stop drain can drop a hook already answered 204 (receivers not closed before try_recv).

I5 deploy exclusion via an OS file lock (File::try_lock on cctg.deploy-lock, released when the process dies) plus a deploy id file echoed in the result, instead of a create_new lock file (stale after a killed deploy) or a nonce derived from candidate size+mtime.

I1: a candidate that cannot be deleted or renamed away is remembered by size+mtime and not re-taken until it changes, rather than retrying it with a backoff; deploy already refuses while cctg.next waits, so only a hand-made change re-arms it.
